title: B Box Projections
statementMd:
Box Projections
      Input ﬁle:          standard input
      Output ﬁle:         standard output

For a positive integer d, let [d] = {1, 2, . . . , d}. You are given three positive integers a, b, c.

Consider a set S ⊆ [a] × [b] × [c] of integer triples. It must satisfy all of the following conditions:


     • for every (x, y) ∈ [a] × [b], at least one triple (x, y, z) belongs to S;

     • for every (x, z) ∈ [a] × [c], at least one triple (x, y, z) belongs to S;

     • for every (y, z) ∈ [b] × [c], at least one triple (x, y, z) belongs to S.


In other words, deleting any one coordinate from the triples in S must produce every possible pair of the
other two coordinates. Determine the minimum possible value of |S|.

Input
The ﬁrst line contains an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 100), the number of test cases.

For each test case, one line contains three integers a, b, c (1 ≤ a ≤ 100, 1 ≤ b ≤ 100, 1 ≤ c ≤ 100).

Output
For each test case, output one line containing a single integer, the minimum possible |S|.

Example
                   standard input                                         standard output
 2                                                       4
 2 2 2                                                   12
 4 3 2

Note
For (a, b, c) = (2, 2, 2), one possible choice of S is:

                                     S = {(1, 1, 1), (1, 2, 2), (2, 1, 2), (2, 2, 1)}


For (a, b, c) = (4, 3, 2), one possible choice of S is:

                                          S = {(1, 1, 1), (1, 2, 1), (1, 3, 2),
                                                 (2, 1, 1), (2, 2, 2), (2, 3, 1),
                                                 (3, 1, 2), (3, 2, 2), (3, 3, 1),
                                                 (4, 1, 2), (4, 2, 1), (4, 3, 2)}
